quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Under the National Association of Rocketry (NAR) Model Rocket Safety Code, how must a model rocket be constructed and launched?
quiz_item.question: Under the National Association of Rocketry (NAR) Model Rocket Safety Code, how must a model rocket be constructed and launched?
options: A. Build the airframe from lightweight steel tubing and ignite the engine with a hand-held match before stepping back five feet.
B. Pack the parachute directly against the motor nozzle without recovery wadding and launch into low clouds to test altitude.
C. Aim the launch rod horizontally at a 30-degree angle to clear nearby trees and power lines.

D. Use only lightweight non-metallic materials (paper, wood, plastic), install flame-resistant recovery wadding, verify a clear sky and safe standoff distance, and launch electrically using a controller with a removable safety interlock key.

First Commercial Astronaut Wings: Its test pilots earned the first commercial astronaut wings, award by the FAA in 2004 (p. 23).

Step 3 - Trace SpaceX Founding Goals: Elon Musk (1971- ) formed Space Exploration Technologies (Space X) in 2002 to build rockets that could inexpensively carry payloads to low Earth orbit (p. 23).
Step 4 - Document Dragon Cargo Missions: After years of successful rocket launches, the company began transporting cargo to the International Space Station in October 2012 in its Dragon (p. 23).

C. Aim the launch rod horizontally at a 30-degree angle to clear nearby trees and power lines.

choices: A. Build the airframe from lightweight steel tubing and ignite the engine with a hand-held match before stepping back five feet.

options: A. Astronomy, planetary geology, or meteorology.
B. Commercial aviation piloting and air traffic management.
C. Architecture, industrial design, or chemical metallurgy.
D. Electrical, electronics, mechanical, or civil engineering.
choices: A. Astronomy, planetary geology, or meteorology.
B. Commercial aviation piloting and air traffic management.
C. Architecture, industrial design, or chemical metallurgy.
D. Electrical, electronics, mechanical, or civil engineering.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Electrical, electronics, mechanical, or civil engineering.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Most engineers in the space industry earn degrees in electrical, electronics, mechanical, or civil engineering, and many specialize in propulsion, structures, navigation, or communications (p. 93).
